title: Where do April and July sit when columns become a line?
description: The April and July columns of Kerala's temperature graph turn into two dots, each at the top of its column, joined by a line in month order. The video reads the height of each dot and how far the line falls, then answers Keeko's doubt that a later month makes the line climb.
teaching_notes: One idea: a dot sits at the top of its column, and the line between two dots shows the change. Watch for students who think a later month must make the line go up.

source: Kerala's April column reaches about 33 degrees and its July
video_script.why: The child can read a column graph but has not yet seen that a line graph holds the same readings as dots joined in month order.
video_script.substitution: Put a dot at the top of each column, join the dots in month order, then read whether the line goes up or down and by how much.
video_script.anchor: the book's graph of the monthly maximum temperature in Kerala
video_script.wrong_answer: the line climbs up from April to July
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks a later month sits higher, so the line climbs from April to July; a later month only moves the dot to the right.
video_script.payoff_line: the line slopes down by about four degrees

final_answer.value: April's dot at about 33, July's at about 29; the line slopes down by about 4 degrees
final_answer.spoken: April's dot sits at about thirty three, July's at about twenty nine, and the line slopes down by about four degrees

never_show: a line climbing from April to July
maths_rules: Kerala, monthly maximum temperature in 2023: April column about 33 degrees Celsius, July column about 29 degrees Celsius
each dot sits at the top of its column: April dot at about 33, July dot at about 29
dots are joined in month order; July is to the right of April and lower
slip: a later month is further right, not higher; the height comes only from the reading
video_script.design: One idea: a dot at the top of each column, joined in month order, makes the line. The wrong idea is that a later month makes the line climb. The Kerala graph stays on screen all video; the columns fade into dots in the ground part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='cols'/>A column graph shows the highest temperature of each month in Kerala.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>April's column reaches about thirty three degrees Celsius. July's column reaches about twenty nine degrees.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>If we draw a line instead of columns, where do these two months sit? What does the line between them show?

<bookmark mark='lg'/>A graph made of dots joined by lines is called a line graph.
<bookmark mark='use'/>Line graphs are used to show how something changes across time.

<bookmark mark='vals'/>April's dot sits at about thirty three. July's dot sits at about twenty nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>From April to July, the line slopes down by about four degrees.
April's dot sits at about thirty three, and July's dot sits at about twenty nine.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the line climbs up from April to July, because July comes later in the year.
<bookmark mark='right'/>But a later month only moves the dot further to the right.
<bookmark mark='read'/>How high the dot sits comes from the reading, and July's reading is lower than April's.
